alex: Quick follow-up from the defrag/offload RFC — brains needed. I ran the staging perf tests with the compact-on-evict tweak and saw lower tail latency but worse long-run fragmentation. Can we decide if we want a hybrid: compact-as-you-go + fragmentation-aware slab merge?

jamie: can you paste the perf numbers?

alex: TL;DR: p99 down 12%, p50 same, steady-state rescans up ~8% and free-run fragmentation metric +15%.

lee: sounds like the compact helps latency for hot runs but increases churn that makes small allocs suffer later. What if we gate compacting to slab hotness > 0.75 and only merge slabs when contiguous free > threshold?

jamie: i like gating. how do we expose that threshold? runtime flag or allocator API?

lee: allocator API so private still works. proposal: add a "merge_hint" on dealloc path: {"slab_id": int, "free_ratio": float}. runtime can call merge when neighboring slabs cross the threshold.

sara: also need telemetry before we flip this in prod. we should track: slab_count, avg_free_chunk_size, contiguous_free_fraction, compaction_ops/sec, and mutation latency during compaction.

alex: agreed. also need fallbacks for Dedicated when memory pressure is high. We can't block inference threads. So compaction must be cooperative and preemptible.

lee: prototype API sketch:

```
// allocator.h
struct MergeHint { uint32_t slab_id; float free_ratio; };
// on free path
void allocator_free(void* p, MergeHint* hint /* optional */);
// background
void background_try_merge(MergeHint hint);
```

jamie: for cooperative preemption, background_try_merge should check a budget token and yield after N pages moved. token is replenished by workload slack. :thinking:

ops-bot: test-run 2026-03-20T18:12Z: staging-compact-hybrid v1 -> 3/5 tests passed (OOM on small-alloc-sanity). See /ci/1234

alex: Ugh. OOM repro on small-alloc-sanity. likely due to delayed merges + compact pushing fragmentation to smaller bins.

sara: can we add a lightweight proactive small-bin refill that converts some contiguous free into small-chunks instead of full-slab merges? cheaper and keeps small allocs happy.

lee: yes — a refill path that does a quick split of larger free runs into small chunk slabs. No full relocation. That reduces compaction pressure.

jamie: sounds good. action items: 1) implement MergeHint API (lee) 2) telemetry dashboard + alerts for contiguous_free_fraction drop (sara) 3) small-bin-refill POC (alex) 4) budgeted background compaction tokens + scheduler (jamie).

alex: timeline? aiming for canary next week. if telemetry looks healthy we roll to 25% then 100%.

sara: i'll add dashboard tiles and a regression eval (prompt-serving + embedder microbench).

lee: i'll open a PR with API + unit tests. keep interface backwards compatible: allocator_free can accept null hint.

jamie: don't forget to add per-tenant config toggles for Dedicated (customers may want to pin behavior).

alex: good call. mention in the PR description. ok team, let's sync tomorrow 10am syncroom if we have early numbers. :thumbsup:

lee: noted. ping me on thread if the OOM repro steps land in CI.

alex: thanks — closing for now.
